chapter: Melvin Moore, Hammond and the New York trip
title: Hobart Banks stays home; Rozelle Claxton replaces him
summary: Hobart will not leave his family for five years, so Fields hires Claxton through the Kansas City union.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And so, that's the way we left. So I talked it over with the guys, did they want to go, and all of them were--they were just tickled to death. Hobart Banks said I don't know, I'll let you know; so I said what is wrong? Did you say that was five years? I said yeah. He said, I don't know if I can be gone from my old lady for five years, so I said (inaudible).
He thought the wife was going to stay back in Tulsa for the whole five years?

Yeah. So I said I don't know and so the rest of the guys said yeah and Hobart said I'll let you know. So anyway, we went on and the next few days we had another gig, I said I'm going to send this contract back to Alexander and I wanted to know what you think, Hobart; no, Fish, I'm not going. He went on to tell me about how old his little boy was and I just hate to leave there and the old lady and all, I just don't think I'll make it. So I said okay but I'm not turning it down. He said I don't blame you--
Yeah, Hobart Banks. So I went and called Kansas City, called the union, and wanted to know if there was anybody they could recommend, you know, a piano player, and you know I always dwelled on

that reading, and they said yes, there's one young man, if he's interested, Rozelle Claxton, he'll play anything you want and he's a nice arranger. So I got his number and I called Rozelle, and he accepted. He said you're going to New York? I said yeah, and he said what are you paying? I said Rozelle, we don't work for anything less than scale around here, but I don't know what it's going to be there, I don't know what kind of gigs they're going to put me on, but you ask anybody about my reputation and you'll get the benefit of the doubt if we get into the money. He said just so I'm getting out of this area, I'm with you. I told him to come right on.
